title: A child on the throne
hookLine: Duleep Singh, a small boy, becomes Maharaja, with his mother as regent

lines: A SMALL BOY LED TO THE THRONE.
GROWN MEN BOW TO A CHILD.
cards: A small boy is led to the throne of the Punjab. His feet don't reach the floor from the cushion. Around him stand grown men who have just watched a Maharaja, a prince and a chief minister die, and who now bow to a child.
Beside him, watching all of them, sits his mother. The boy is Duleep Singh, the youngest son of Ranjit Singh. The woman is Maharani Jind Kaur.

teach.b: After yesterday's killings, the men who held the army needed a Maharaja they could manage. Hira Singh, the dead minister's son, raised the boy Duleep Singh to the throne and ruled as chief minister in his name.
A child king is easy to seat on a throne; that was part of the point.
Jind Kaur stood beside her son as regent, and she was no quiet figure. Histories describe her as sharp and strong-willed.
Hira Singh did not last long; he too fell in the court's quarrels, and in time her own brother, Jawahar Singh, became chief minister.
A child can't command an army or read a treaty, and everyone around him had a plan for his name. The ministers wanted it to rule by. The army wanted it to fight under.
The British, watching from across the river, wanted to know who really held the power.

teach.h: MANY HANDS REACHING FOR ONE NAME.
teach.b: A boy on a throne is a name with many hands reaching for it.

teach.h: THE LORD AS FATHER AND MOTHER.
teach.b: In a hymn of Guru Arjan, the Lord is called father and mother, kin and brother, and protector in every place, so what is there to fear?
It's the safety a small child feels when someone greater is watching. Duleep Singh had a throne, a mother and a court. What he needed most was someone who wanted nothing from him.

how: Sikhs remember Maharaja Duleep Singh, enthroned as a child with his mother, Maharani Jind Kaur, as regent, and his story is told in Sikh homes and gurdwaras.

o: the youngest son, made Maharaja as a small boy
the eldest son, who ruled the Punjab for decades
a minister who governed in the Maharaja's name

games.q: the boy and the court — tap the pairs.

s: Duleep Singh came to the throne as a grown man
he was a small boy, with his mother beside him as regent.
Jind Kaur was a quiet figure at court
histories describe her as sharp and strong-willed, and her brother became chief minister.
in Guru Arjan's hymn the Lord is called father and mother
and kin, brother and protector in every place, so there is nothing to fear.

games.q: you're a minister after the killings. the court needs a new Maharaja, one the ministers can manage. what does the court do?
o: enthrone the youngest son, a small boy, and rule in his name.
games.why: Hira Singh raised the boy Duleep Singh to the throne and ruled as chief minister, with Jind Kaur beside her son.

practice: Bring to mind one child you know, or the child you once were, small in a room full of busy, loud grown-ups.
Now picture one adult turning toward them, kneeling to their height, wanting nothing except that they're all right, and stay with that picture, breathing slowly.
If you pray, you can say Waheguru on each breath out, holding that child in mind.
